title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 349 (Official Liquidator to make payments into public account of India)

content.overview: Every Official Liquidator shall, in such manner and at such times as may be prescribed, pay the monies received by him as Official Liquidator of any company into the public account of India in the Reserve Bank of India.
content.glance: Official Liquidator must pay monies received into the public account of India in the RBI as prescribed.
content.study: Section 349 is a mandatory banking direction for Official Liquidators. Every Official Liquidator must pay the monies received by him as Official Liquidator of any company into the public account of India in the Reserve Bank of India, in the manner and at the times prescribed. The rule secures public accountability for funds held in that capacity.

sections.heading: Payment into public account
sections.body: Official Liquidator must pay monies received into the public account of India in the RBI in the prescribed manner and times.

examples.title: Receipt of realisation
examples.body: An Official Liquidator realises assets of a company in liquidation. He must deposit the proceeds into the public account of India in the RBI under s. 349.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 349 apply to a Company Liquidator who is not an Official Liquidator?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 349 is addressed to every Official Liquidator. Company Liquidators are governed by the deposit rules in s. 350.

misconceptions.trap: Any liquidator may keep funds in a private account.
misconceptions.correction: Official Liquidators must pay into the public account of India in the RBI; Company Liquidators must use a scheduled-bank special account under s. 350.
